summary:
Martian Map is an interactive tool for the scientific and geographic exploration of Mars that integrates and links information from various space missions, instruments, research studies, and scientific sources.

Its purpose is to facilitate understanding of the characteristics of Martian regions and the associated scientific research through two complementary modes of exploration: by geographic region and by scientific question.

To demonstrate how it works, a case study will be conducted in Mawrth Vallis (Mars Science Laboratory candidate landing ellipse), focusing on the exploration of mineralogical and geological evidence related to the history of water on Mars. The tool will allow users to access contextualized information, identify available data and its limitations, and visualize and analyze exploration routes based on existing information.
details:
Mars Map: Mawrth Vallis is an interactive scientific and geographic exploration web platform designed to analyze high-resolution orbital datasets, stratigraphic boundaries, and landing safety parameters in the Mawrth Vallis region on Mars.

How it Works & Key Features:

The platform operates on a robust three-state architecture (Home Landing, Regional Mode, and Investigation Mode):

1. Regional Mode (Route 1): Features an interactive USGS/MOLA map with dynamic layer controls (Regions and Mola Footprints) allowing users to set Point A and Point B trajectory vectors, calculate geodesic distances, and synchronize overlapping orbital datasets in real-time. It includes automated data export to CSV and mineral composition breakdown charts (Unaltered, Al-rich clays, Fe/Mg Mawrth, and Fe/Mg Oxia).

2. Investigation Mode (Route 2): Focuses on core scientific research questions regarding aqueous history and clay mineralogy, correlating stratigraphic layers with transitability and landing ellipse constraints.

Benefits & Expected Impact:

The platform bridges the gap between raw planetary data and accessible scientific visualization. By integrating NASA/USGS spatial datasets with Supabase and PostGIS, it empowers researchers, educators, and space enthusiasts to evaluate landing safety, wheel wear coefficients, and mineralogical distributions rapidly and intuitively.

Tech Stack & Tools:

- Frontend: React, Vite, TypeScript, Leaflet.js, HTML5/CSS3 (with custom atmospheric/crater textures).

- Backend & Database: Supabase, PostgreSQL / PostGIS.

- Datasets & APIs: NASA USGS planetary maps, MOLA topography, CRISM/CTX footprints, and NASA ODE archives.

Creativity & Team Approach:

Our approach merges rigorous planetary science with immersive UI design, featuring a custom Martian-themed aesthetic. The project carefully addresses information gaps, high-resolution DTM constraints, and spectral interpolations to deliver an authentic mission-planning experience.
